findings.title: Settings-in-slice blind spot is acknowledged, not hidden
findings.description: The design explicitly calls out in its Risk Assessment that a slice which edits `.squadron.toml` settings won't show `limits_changed` or `exclusions_changed` between two exports, because both boundaries are measured under the live checkout's settings (D5). This is a known limitation of the "read settings from live checkout" approach, not a hidden dependency. The architecture doesn't require detecting in-slice settings changes, and the design states each record records which settings it used. This is correctly characterized as a risk with a stated mitigation (breaks fire against earlier snapshots taken under different settings), so no action is required.
